job.style: a short story with Indian characters in everyday life

response.passage: Rohan and his sister Meera were playing in their garden in Bengaluru. Rohan pushed his toy car across the flat patio, and it rolled at a steady pace in a straight line. Meera watched it and said, 'It is moving at a constant speed because it covers equal distances in equal intervals of time.' Later, they went to the park to watch a swing. Meera noticed that whether she pulled the swing back a little or a lot, the time taken for one complete back-and-forth movement remained the same. She explained, 'The time period of a pendulum does not depend on the amplitude of the swing.' Nearby, their father was jogging. He ran 2 kilometers in 20 minutes. Rohan calculated his father's speed by dividing the distance of 2 kilometers by the time of 1/3 of an hour, resulting in 6 kilometers per hour. He noted that even a slow-moving snail has a measurable speed. Finally, they looked at a distance-time graph in Rohan’s textbook. A horizontal line on the graph showed that the distance from the starting point did not change over time, meaning the object was at rest, not moving at all.
response.summary: Rohan and Meera learn about the physics of motion by observing a toy car, a swing, and a jogger. They discover how to correctly calculate speed and interpret distance-time graphs.
